newsitem.title: GERMANY: BASF gets conditional US ok for Meridia drug.
newsitem.headline: BASF gets conditional US ok for Meridia drug.

text.p: German chemicals group BASF AG said on Monday the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) had given it conditional approval to market its Meridia TM obesity drug in the U.S.
BASF said in a statement that the FDA had sent it an "Approvable Letter" -- an announcement of approval provided that certain conditions are met.
The news marks a turnaround after a U.S. advisory committee in September recommended that the FDA withhold approval for Meridia.
BASF gets conditional US ok for Meridia drug
Knoll Pharmaceutical Company (KPC), BASF's U.S. subsidiary, will be able to market Meridia in the U.S. after the FDA gives its final approval, BASF said.
It said final approval would be given after agreement had been reached on product labelling and the instruction leaflet and on a programme of clinical tests during Phase IV marketing.
BASF has said it expects Meridia to post sales of $200 million to $400 million annually.
"We are delighted that the approval of Meridia has progressed so far," Knoll Pharmaceutical President Carter Eckert said in a statement.
"Obesity is a chronic disease whose effects cause about 300,000 deaths per year in the U.S. alone."

Members of the Endocrinologic and Metabolic Drugs Advisory Committee had said in September that the anti-obesity capsules were effective but said they still had a number of questions about its safety.
